text.zh: Which of the following is the core focus of the Governance (G) dimension in the ESG framework?
Corporate carbon emission reduction
Corporate treatment of employees and communities
Corporate board structure, management mechanisms and internal controls
Corporate product safety and customer rights protection

explanation.zh: *The Governance (G) dimension of ESG mainly focuses on the internal management and supervision mechanism of enterprises, including board structure, management efficiency, internal control system, information disclosure, etc. A belongs to the Environmental (E) dimension, B and D belong to the Social (S) dimension.

text.zh: Which of the following is NOT a key indicator of the Governance (G) dimension?
Board independence
Executive compensation structure
Employee turnover rate
Information disclosure quality

explanation.zh: *Employee turnover rate is a key indicator of the Social (S) dimension, reflecting the level of enterprise employee management. A, B, and D are all core indicators of the Governance (G) dimension, involving board governance, incentive mechanism and information transparency.

text.zh: What does "board independence" in the Governance (G) dimension mainly refer to?
The board of directors is completely independent of the enterprise's management
The board of directors includes a certain number of independent directors who are not affiliated with the enterprise and can make objective decisions
The board of directors has the right to independently decide all matters of the enterprise without shareholder supervision
The board of directors is independent of the enterprise's shareholders

explanation.zh: *Board independence mainly means that the board of directors includes independent directors who have no direct or indirect interest relationship with the enterprise, its major shareholders or management. These independent directors can objectively evaluate and supervise the operation of the enterprise and protect the interests of all shareholders. A, C, and D are one-sided understandings of board independence.

text.zh: Which of the following is an important role of independent directors in corporate governance?
Participate in the daily operation and management of the enterprise
Supervise the behavior of management and prevent the abuse of power
Decide the salary and welfare of the enterprise's employees
Formulate the enterprise's marketing strategy

explanation.zh: *The core role of independent directors is to supervise the operation of the management, ensure that the enterprise's decision-making is fair and transparent, protect the interests of minority shareholders, and prevent the management from abusing power for personal gain. A, C, and D are the responsibilities of the enterprise's management, not independent directors.

text.zh: What is the main purpose of establishing a corporate internal control system?
Reduce the enterprise's operating costs
Ensure the authenticity and integrity of financial information, and prevent operational risks
Improve the enterprise's market competitiveness
Speed up the enterprise's decision-making efficiency

explanation.zh: *The core purpose of the internal control system is to standardize the enterprise's business processes, ensure the authenticity, completeness and accuracy of financial information, prevent and control operational risks, compliance risks and financial risks, and ensure the healthy operation of the enterprise. A, C, and D are not the main purposes of the internal control system.

text.zh: Which of the following is a key component of the corporate internal control system?
Employee training system
Risk assessment and control mechanism
Customer service system
Supplier management system

explanation.zh: *The key components of the internal control system include risk assessment, control activities, information and communication, internal supervision, etc. The risk assessment and control mechanism is the core part, which is used to identify, assess and respond to the risks faced by the enterprise. A, C, and D are auxiliary management systems of the enterprise, not core components of internal control.

text.zh: What does "executive compensation governance" in the Governance (G) dimension refer to?
Setting the highest salary limit for enterprise executives
Formulating a scientific and reasonable executive compensation system that is linked to performance and can stimulate executives to create value
Ensuring that the executive salary is higher than the industry average
Letting executives independently decide their own salary

explanation.zh: *Executive compensation governance focuses on establishing a fair and transparent compensation system, linking executive compensation with the enterprise's operating performance, long-term development and risk control, so as to balance the interests of executives, shareholders and the enterprise, and stimulate executives to work hard for the long-term development of the enterprise. A, C, and D do not conform to the concept of executive compensation governance.

text.zh: Which of the following is a reasonable executive compensation structure?
Only fixed salary, no performance bonus
Fixed salary + performance bonus + long-term incentive (such as equity incentives)
Only performance bonus, no fixed salary
Fixed salary + arbitrary bonus decided by the board of directors

explanation.zh: *A reasonable executive compensation structure should combine short-term and long-term incentives. Fixed salary ensures the basic income of executives, performance bonus links with short-term operating performance, and long-term incentives (such as equity incentives) link executives' interests with the long-term development of the enterprise, which can effectively avoid short-term behaviors of executives. A, C, and D are unreasonable compensation structures.

text.zh: What is the meaning of "information disclosure" in corporate governance?
Disclosing all internal information of the enterprise to the public
Disclosing the enterprise's financial information, operating information, risk information and other important information to shareholders and the public in a timely, accurate and complete manner
Disclosing only positive information of the enterprise, and hiding negative information
Disclosing information only to major shareholders, not to minority shareholders

explanation.zh: *Information disclosure is one of the core requirements of corporate governance, which requires enterprises to disclose important information such as financial status, operating results, risk factors, and corporate governance structure to all stakeholders (shareholders, investors, regulators, etc.) in a timely, accurate, complete and transparent manner, so as to protect the right to know of stakeholders. A, C, and D are not the correct understanding of information disclosure.

text.zh: Which of the following is an important content of corporate information disclosure?
Employee personal information
Financial statements and operating reports
Enterprise's internal meeting minutes
Supplier's trade secrets

explanation.zh: *Financial statements and operating reports are the core content of corporate information disclosure, which can reflect the enterprise's financial status, operating results and cash flow, helping stakeholders understand the operation of the enterprise. A, C, and D are either internal information that does not need to be disclosed or information involving privacy and trade secrets, which should not be disclosed arbitrarily.

text.zh: What is the impact of insufficient information disclosure on enterprises?
Reducing the enterprise's operating costs
Improving the trust of investors and the public in the enterprise
Increasing the enterprise's financing costs and facing regulatory penalties
Enhancing the enterprise's market competitiveness

explanation.zh: *Insufficient information disclosure will make investors and the public unable to fully understand the true situation of the enterprise, reduce investor confidence, increase the difficulty and cost of enterprise financing, and may also violate the requirements of regulators, leading to fines and other penalties. A, B, and D are opposite to the actual impact.

text.zh: Which of the following is a measure to improve the quality of corporate information disclosure?
Delaying the disclosure of important information
Establishing a standardized information disclosure system and improving the accuracy and completeness of information
Hiding negative information of the enterprise
Disclosing false information to beautify the enterprise's operating situation

explanation.zh: *Establishing a standardized information disclosure system, clarifying the scope, time and requirements of disclosure, strengthening the review of disclosed information, and ensuring the accuracy, completeness and timeliness of information are effective measures to improve the quality of information disclosure. A, C, and D are acts that damage the quality of information disclosure and violate relevant regulations.

text.zh: What is the core responsibility of the board of directors in corporate governance?
Responsible for the daily operation and management of the enterprise
Formulate the enterprise's development strategy, supervise the management, and protect the interests of shareholders
Responsible for the enterprise's financial accounting work
Responsible for the enterprise's marketing and sales work

explanation.zh: *The core responsibility of the board of directors is to formulate the long-term development strategy and major decision-making of the enterprise, supervise the performance of the management, ensure that the enterprise's operation is in line with the interests of shareholders, and assume the fiduciary responsibility to shareholders. A, C, and D are the responsibilities of the enterprise's management team, not the board of directors.

text.zh: Which of the following is a key indicator to evaluate the effectiveness of the board of directors?
The number of board meetings held each year
The proportion of independent directors in the board of directors
The age structure of the board members
The educational background of the board members

explanation.zh: *The proportion of independent directors is a key indicator to evaluate the effectiveness of the board of directors. A higher proportion of independent directors can better play the supervisory role of the board, improve the objectivity and fairness of decision-making, and protect the interests of minority shareholders. A, C, and D are auxiliary indicators and cannot directly reflect the effectiveness of the board of directors.

text.zh: What is the role of the board of supervisors in corporate governance?
Participate in the formulation of the enterprise's development strategy
Supervise the board of directors and management, and ensure that the enterprise's operation complies with laws, regulations and the articles of association
Responsible for the enterprise's human resource management
Formulate the enterprise's internal control system

explanation.zh: *The board of supervisors is an important supervision body in corporate governance, whose core role is to supervise the performance of the board of directors and management, check the enterprise's financial information, and ensure that the enterprise's operation complies with national laws, regulations and the enterprise's articles of association, so as to protect the interests of the enterprise and shareholders. A, C, and D are not the responsibilities of the board of supervisors.

text.zh: Which of the following is a responsibility of the board of supervisors?
Approving the enterprise's annual financial budget and final accounts
Investigating and dealing with the illegal and irregular behaviors of the board of directors and management
Deciding the appointment and removal of the enterprise's senior management
Formulating the enterprise's marketing strategy

explanation.zh: *The board of supervisors has the right to supervise the board of directors and management, and if it finds illegal, irregular or dereliction of duty behaviors, it has the right to investigate and put forward suggestions for handling. A, C, and D are the powers of the board of directors, not the board of supervisors.

text.zh: What does "shareholder rights protection" in corporate governance refer to?
Only protecting the interests of major shareholders
Protecting the legitimate rights and interests of all shareholders, including the right to vote, the right to profit, and the right to know
Protecting the interests of shareholders at the expense of the interests of other stakeholders
Letting shareholders directly participate in the daily operation of the enterprise

explanation.zh: *Shareholder rights protection is an important part of corporate governance, which requires enterprises to respect and protect the legitimate rights and interests of all shareholders (including major shareholders and minority shareholders), including the right to vote at shareholders' meetings, the right to share profits, the right to know enterprise information, and the right to appeal against illegal behaviors. A, C, and D are not the correct understanding of shareholder rights protection.

text.zh: Which of the following is a measure to protect the rights and interests of minority shareholders?
Restricting the voting rights of minority shareholders
Ensuring that minority shareholders have equal access to enterprise information
Ignoring the opinions and suggestions of minority shareholders
Giving priority to the interests of major shareholders in profit distribution

explanation.zh: *Ensuring that minority shareholders have equal access to enterprise information, equal voting rights, and the right to put forward proposals at shareholders' meetings are important measures to protect the rights and interests of minority shareholders. A, C, and D are acts that damage the rights and interests of minority shareholders.

text.zh: What is the meaning of "corporate governance structure" in ESG?
The organizational structure of the enterprise's management team
A set of institutional arrangements that regulate the relationships between shareholders, the board of directors, the board of supervisors and the management
The internal departmental setting of the enterprise
The relationship between the enterprise and its suppliers and customers

explanation.zh: *Corporate governance structure is a set of institutional arrangements to clarify the rights and responsibilities of shareholders, the board of directors, the board of supervisors and the management, and regulate the decision-making, supervision and execution mechanisms of the enterprise, so as to ensure the standardized operation of the enterprise and protect the interests of all stakeholders. A, C, and D are not the correct understanding of corporate governance structure.

text.zh: Which of the following is a core component of the corporate governance structure?
The enterprise's production department
The enterprise's marketing department
The board of directors, the board of supervisors and the management
The enterprise's financial department

explanation.zh: *The core components of the corporate governance structure are the three major bodies: the board of directors (decision-making body), the board of supervisors (supervision body) and the management (execution body). These three bodies perform their respective duties and restrict each other to ensure the healthy operation of the enterprise. A, B, and D are functional departments of the enterprise, not core components of the governance structure.

text.zh: What is the impact of a sound corporate governance structure on enterprises?
Increasing the enterprise's operating costs
Reducing the enterprise's decision-making efficiency
Improving the enterprise's operational stability and reducing risks
Reducing the enterprise's market competitiveness

explanation.zh: *A sound corporate governance structure can clarify the rights and responsibilities of each body, standardize the decision-making process, strengthen internal supervision, reduce the risk of management abuse of power, improve the operational stability and anti-risk ability of the enterprise, and help the enterprise achieve long-term development. A, B, and D are opposite to the actual impact.

text.zh: Which of the following is a sign of an imperfect corporate governance structure?
The board of directors includes a sufficient number of independent directors
The management is not supervised by the board of directors and the board of supervisors
The information disclosure is timely and transparent
The rights and interests of minority shareholders are effectively protected

explanation.zh: *An imperfect corporate governance structure is mainly reflected in the lack of effective supervision and restriction mechanisms, such as the management being not supervised by the board of directors and the board of supervisors, which may lead to the abuse of power and damage the interests of the enterprise and shareholders. A, C, and D are signs of a sound corporate governance structure.

text.zh: What does "risk management" in corporate governance refer to?
Avoiding all risks faced by the enterprise
Identifying, assessing, and formulating response strategies for the risks faced by the enterprise to reduce the impact of risks
Ignoring the risks faced by the enterprise and focusing only on operating performance
Transferring all risks of the enterprise to other parties

explanation.zh: *Risk management in corporate governance refers to the enterprise establishing a sound risk management system, identifying and assessing various risks (such as operational risk, financial risk, compliance risk) faced in the process of operation and development, formulating corresponding prevention and control measures and emergency response strategies, so as to minimize the impact of risks on the enterprise. A, C, and D are not the correct understanding of risk management.

text.zh: Which of the following is a key step in corporate risk management?
Risk avoidance: avoiding all business activities that may bring risks
Risk identification: finding out all potential risks faced by the enterprise
Risk ignoring: not taking any measures for identified risks
Risk transfer: transferring all risks to suppliers

explanation.zh: *The key steps of risk management include risk identification, risk assessment, risk response and risk monitoring. Risk identification is the first step, which is to systematically find out all potential risks faced by the enterprise, so as to carry out subsequent assessment and response work. A, C, and D are unreasonable risk management methods.

text.zh: What is the responsibility of the board of directors in corporate risk management?
Implementing the risk management measures formulated by the management
Approving the enterprise's risk management strategy and supervising the implementation of risk management
Responsible for the daily risk control work of the enterprise
Handling specific risk incidents of the enterprise

explanation.zh: *The board of directors is responsible for formulating and approving the enterprise's risk management strategy, determining the risk appetite of the enterprise, and supervising the management to implement risk management measures, so as to ensure that the enterprise's risk management work is carried out in an orderly manner. A, C, and D are the responsibilities of the management, not the board of directors.

text.zh: Which of the following is an example of corporate compliance risk in governance?
The enterprise's product quality does not meet the national standards
The enterprise violates labor laws and regulations and does not pay social insurance for employees
The enterprise does not disclose important information in accordance with regulatory requirements
The enterprise's carbon emissions exceed the standard

explanation.zh: *Compliance risk in corporate governance mainly refers to the risk that the enterprise violates national laws, regulations, regulatory requirements or the enterprise's articles of association in the process of operation, leading to legal liabilities or reputation damage. Not disclosing important information in accordance with regulatory requirements is a typical compliance risk in governance. A and D belong to environmental and social risks, B belongs to social risk.

text.zh: What is the purpose of corporate compliance management?
To meet the requirements of regulators perfunctorily
To ensure that the enterprise's operation complies with laws, regulations and internal rules, and avoid compliance risks
To reduce the enterprise's operating costs
To improve the enterprise's short-term operating performance

explanation.zh: *The purpose of compliance management is to establish a sound compliance management system, standardize the business behaviors of the enterprise and its employees, ensure that all business activities comply with national laws, regulations, regulatory requirements and the enterprise's internal rules and regulations, avoid compliance risks such as legal penalties and reputation damage, and ensure the sustainable operation of the enterprise. A, C, and D are not the purpose of compliance management.

text.zh: Which of the following is a measure for enterprises to strengthen compliance management?
Establishing a compliance management department and formulating a compliance manual
Ignoring the compliance risks in business activities
Encouraging employees to take improper means to pursue performance
Hiding the enterprise's non-compliant behaviors from regulators

explanation.zh: *Establishing a special compliance management department, formulating a compliance manual to clarify the compliance requirements of each business link, and conducting regular compliance training for employees are effective measures to strengthen compliance management. B, C, and D are acts that weaken compliance management and increase compliance risks.

text.zh: What does "director liability" in corporate governance refer to?
Directors are not responsible for the decisions made by the board of directors
Directors are responsible for the decisions made by the board of directors and must perform their duties in good faith and with due diligence
Directors only need to be responsible to major shareholders
Directors can make decisions arbitrarily without considering the interests of the enterprise

explanation.zh: *Director liability refers to the obligation and responsibility that directors must bear when performing their duties. Directors must perform their duties in good faith, with due diligence and in the best interests of the enterprise and all shareholders. If they cause losses to the enterprise due to negligence or intentional acts, they need to bear corresponding legal liabilities. A, C, and D are not the correct understanding of director liability.

text.zh: Which of the following is a situation where directors need to bear legal liability?
Making reasonable decisions in accordance with the law and the articles of association, but the decisions do not achieve the expected results
Neglecting their duties, failing to supervise the management, and causing losses to the enterprise
Expressing different opinions on the decisions of the board of directors and recording them in the meeting minutes
Resigning due to personal reasons before the end of the term of office

explanation.zh: *Directors need to bear legal liability if they fail to perform their duties in good faith and with due diligence, such as neglecting their duties, failing to supervise the management, or making decisions that violate laws and regulations, resulting in losses to the enterprise. A, C, and D are not situations where directors need to bear legal liability.

text.zh: What is the meaning of "corporate code of conduct" in governance?
A set of rules formulated by the enterprise to restrict employees' daily behavior
A set of norms that regulate the behavior of the board of directors, management and employees, and guide the enterprise to operate in a standardized and ethical manner
A set of rules formulated by the enterprise to improve production efficiency
A set of norms that regulate the relationship between the enterprise and its customers

explanation.zh: *The corporate code of conduct is an important part of corporate governance, which covers the board of directors, management, employees and other subjects, clarifies the behavioral norms and ethical requirements in the process of enterprise operation, guides all employees to operate in accordance with laws, regulations and moral norms, and maintains the image and reputation of the enterprise. A, C, and D are one-sided understandings of the corporate code of conduct.

text.zh: Which of the following is an important content of the corporate code of conduct?
Employee dress code
Ethical norms for business activities, anti-corruption and anti-bribery requirements
Enterprise's production process standards
Customer service specifications

explanation.zh: *The core content of the corporate code of conduct includes ethical norms for business activities, anti-corruption and anti-bribery requirements, compliance with laws and regulations, protection of stakeholder interests, etc. These contents are closely related to corporate governance. A, C, and D are auxiliary norms of the enterprise and not core content of the code of conduct in governance.

text.zh: What is the role of the corporate code of conduct in governance?
Restricting the personal freedom of employees
Standardizing the behavior of the enterprise and its employees, reducing operational risks and compliance risks
Increasing the enterprise's operating costs
Reducing the enterprise's decision-making efficiency

explanation.zh: *The corporate code of conduct can standardize the behavior of the board of directors, management and employees, clarify the bottom line of behavior, avoid unethical and non-compliant behaviors, reduce operational risks and compliance risks, and help establish a good corporate image. A, C, and D are opposite to the actual role.

text.zh: Which of the following is a measure to ensure the implementation of the corporate code of conduct?
Formulating the code of conduct but not publicizing it to employees
Establishing a supervision and inspection mechanism to investigate and punish behaviors that violate the code of conduct
Allowing employees to choose whether to abide by the code of conduct
Modifying the code of conduct at will without going through formal procedures

explanation.zh: *To ensure the implementation of the corporate code of conduct, it is necessary to publicize it to all employees, establish a supervision and inspection mechanism, and investigate and punish employees and management who violate the code of conduct, so as to ensure that the code of conduct is effectively implemented. A, C, and D are not conducive to the implementation of the code of conduct.

text.zh: What does "board diversity" in corporate governance refer to?
The board of directors includes members of different genders, ages, educational backgrounds and professional backgrounds
The board of directors includes members from different enterprises
The board of directors includes members of different nationalities
The board of directors includes members with different levels of wealth

explanation.zh: *Board diversity mainly refers to the diversity of the composition of the board of directors, including gender diversity, age diversity, educational background diversity, professional background diversity, etc. A diverse board can bring different perspectives and ideas, improve the quality of decision-making, and better respond to the complex market environment. B, C, and D are only part of board diversity and not the full meaning.

text.zh: What is the benefit of board diversity for enterprises?
Increasing the internal conflicts of the board of directors
Improving the objectivity and comprehensiveness of board decisions
Reducing the efficiency of board meetings
Making the board of directors more difficult to reach a consensus

explanation.zh: *A diverse board of directors has members with different professional backgrounds, experiences and perspectives, which can avoid group thinking, make the board's decision-making more objective, comprehensive and scientific, and help the enterprise better identify risks and seize opportunities. A, C, and D are opposite to the actual benefits.

text.zh: Which of the following is a measure to promote board diversity?
Recruiting board members only from the same industry
Setting quotas for female directors and directors from different professional backgrounds
Recruiting board members only based on personal relationships
Ignoring the diversity of board members and focusing only on professional ability

explanation.zh: *Setting quotas for female directors, directors from different professional backgrounds (such as finance, law, technology) and different age groups, and expanding the scope of board member recruitment are effective measures to promote board diversity. A, C, and D are not conducive to promoting board diversity.

text.zh: What is the meaning of "managerial ownership" in corporate governance?
The management holds all the shares of the enterprise
The management holds a certain proportion of the enterprise's shares, linking their interests with the enterprise's long-term development
The management has the right to decide the enterprise's shareholding structure
The management can freely transfer the enterprise's shares

explanation.zh: *Managerial ownership refers to the situation where the enterprise's senior management holds a certain proportion of the enterprise's shares. This system can link the personal interests of the management with the long-term development and stock price performance of the enterprise, stimulate the management to work hard for the long-term development of the enterprise, and reduce the agency conflict between the management and shareholders. A, C, and D are not the correct understanding of managerial ownership.

text.zh: What is the impact of appropriate managerial ownership on enterprises?
Increasing the agency cost between the management and shareholders
Reducing the management's sense of responsibility for the enterprise
Improving the management's enthusiasm and sense of responsibility, and promoting the long-term development of the enterprise
Leading to the management's pursuit of short-term interests at the expense of long-term development

explanation.zh: *Appropriate managerial ownership can make the management share the risks and benefits of the enterprise, enhance their sense of responsibility and enthusiasm, and encourage them to formulate and implement long-term development strategies, which is conducive to the long-term stable development of the enterprise. A, B, and D are opposite to the actual impact, and excessive managerial ownership may lead to such problems.

text.zh: Which of the following is a problem caused by excessive managerial ownership?
The management pays too much attention to the long-term development of the enterprise
The management controls the board of directors and makes decisions that are not in the interests of minority shareholders
The management's enthusiasm for work is reduced
The enterprise's financing difficulty increases

explanation.zh: *Excessive managerial ownership may make the management hold too much power, control the board of directors and decision-making power, and even make decisions that are beneficial to themselves but not in the interests of minority shareholders, which damages the rights and interests of minority shareholders and affects the fairness of corporate governance. A, C, and D are not problems caused by excessive managerial ownership.

text.zh: What is the meaning of "proxy voting" in shareholder rights protection?
Shareholders entrust others to exercise their voting rights at shareholders' meetings on their behalf
Shareholders give up their voting rights
Major shareholders exercise the voting rights of minority shareholders without authorization
Shareholders vote online without attending the shareholders' meeting

explanation.zh: *Proxy voting is an important way to protect shareholders' rights and interests, especially minority shareholders. It refers to shareholders who are unable to attend the shareholders' meeting in person entrusting a proxy (such as other shareholders, lawyers) to exercise their voting rights in accordance with the entrustment, so as to ensure that shareholders can exercise their voting rights normally. B, C, and D are not the correct understanding of proxy voting.

text.zh: Which of the following is a requirement for proxy voting?
The proxy must be a shareholder of the enterprise
The shareholder must issue a written entrustment document to the proxy
The proxy can exercise voting rights beyond the scope of the entrustment
The proxy can decide the voting direction at will without the shareholder's authorization

explanation.zh: *Proxy voting requires shareholders to issue a formal written entrustment document, clarifying the scope of entrustment (such as which proposals to vote on, how to vote) and the validity period of the entrustment. The proxy must exercise voting rights in accordance with the entrustment document and cannot exceed the scope of entrustment or decide the voting direction at will. A, C, and D do not conform to the requirements of proxy voting.

text.zh: What is the role of proxy voting in corporate governance?
Helping major shareholders control the shareholders' meeting
Ensuring that all shareholders, especially minority shareholders, can exercise their voting rights
Reducing the participation of shareholders in the governance of the enterprise
Making the decision-making of the shareholders' meeting more arbitrary

explanation.zh: *Proxy voting solves the problem that shareholders cannot attend the shareholders' meeting in person due to time, distance and other reasons, ensuring that all shareholders (including minority shareholders) can exercise their voting rights, participate in the decision-making of the enterprise, and protect their legitimate rights and interests. A, C, and D are opposite to the actual role.

text.zh: What does "corporate governance rating" refer to?
The rating of the enterprise's operating performance by financial institutions
The evaluation of the enterprise's corporate governance level by professional institutions, reflecting the effectiveness of the enterprise's governance
The rating of the enterprise's product quality by consumers
The rating of the enterprise's environmental performance by environmental protection departments

explanation.zh: *Corporate governance rating is an evaluation of the enterprise's corporate governance level (including board structure, internal control, information disclosure, shareholder rights protection, etc.) by professional rating institutions. The rating result can reflect the effectiveness of the enterprise's governance and provide reference for investors, regulators and other stakeholders. A, C, and D are not corporate governance ratings.

text.zh: Which of the following is a key indicator for corporate governance rating?
Enterprise's sales volume
Enterprise's profit margin
Board independence and information disclosure quality
Enterprise's employee satisfaction

explanation.zh: *The key indicators for corporate governance rating mainly include board structure (such as the proportion of independent directors), internal control effectiveness, information disclosure quality, shareholder rights protection, executive compensation governance, etc. A and B are economic indicators, D is a social indicator, which are not key indicators for governance rating.

text.zh: What is the impact of a high corporate governance rating on enterprises?
Increasing the enterprise's operating costs
Reducing the enterprise's financing costs and improving investor confidence
Reducing the enterprise's market competitiveness
Increasing the enterprise's regulatory risks

explanation.zh: *A high corporate governance rating indicates that the enterprise's governance structure is sound, internal control is effective, and information disclosure is transparent, which can improve the trust of investors and regulators in the enterprise, reduce the difficulty and cost of financing, and enhance the enterprise's long-term competitiveness. A, C, and D are opposite to the actual impact.

text.zh: Which of the following is a measure to improve the corporate governance rating?
Reducing the number of independent directors
Strengthening internal control and improving information disclosure quality
Hiding negative information of the enterprise
Reducing the supervision of the management

explanation.zh: *Strengthening the construction of internal control system, improving the transparency and completeness of information disclosure, optimizing the board structure, and protecting the rights and interests of shareholders are effective measures to improve the corporate governance rating. A, C, and D will reduce the corporate governance rating.

text.zh: What is the meaning of "agency problem" in corporate governance?
The conflict of interests between the enterprise and its suppliers
The conflict of interests between the enterprise and its customers
The conflict of interests between shareholders (owners) and management (agents) due to different goals
The conflict of interests between major shareholders and minority shareholders

explanation.zh: *The agency problem in corporate governance refers to the conflict of interests between shareholders (owners of the enterprise) and management (agents entrusted by shareholders to manage the enterprise). Shareholders pursue the maximization of enterprise value, while management may pursue personal interests (such as high salary, job stability) at the expense of shareholder interests, resulting in agency costs. A, B, and D are not agency problems in the narrow sense.

text.zh: Which of the following is an example of the agency problem?
The management invests in high-risk projects to pursue short-term performance and ignores long-term risks
The board of directors approves a reasonable development strategy for the enterprise
The management works hard to improve the enterprise's operating performance
The board of supervisors supervises the management effectively

explanation.zh: *The management investing in high-risk projects to pursue short-term performance (so as to obtain high performance bonuses) but ignoring the long-term risks of the enterprise is a typical agency problem. This behavior is beneficial to the management's personal interests but may damage the interests of shareholders. B, C, and D are not examples of agency problems.

text.zh: What is a measure to solve the agency problem in corporate governance?
Reducing the supervision of the management
Establishing an effective incentive and restraint mechanism for the management
Letting the management independently decide their own salary
Ignoring the behavior of the management

explanation.zh: *Establishing an effective incentive and restraint mechanism is the core measure to solve the agency problem. The incentive mechanism (such as equity incentives) links the management's interests with the enterprise's long-term value, and the restraint mechanism (such as board supervision, internal control) restricts the management's behavior, so as to align the goals of the management and shareholders. A, C, and D cannot solve the agency problem, but will aggravate it.

text.zh: What is the meaning of "internal audit" in corporate governance?
The audit of the enterprise's financial statements by external audit institutions
The independent audit of the enterprise's internal control, financial activities and operational activities by the enterprise's internal audit department
The audit of the enterprise's employees by the human resources department
The audit of the enterprise's suppliers by the procurement department

explanation.zh: *Internal audit is an important part of corporate governance, which is an independent and objective supervision and evaluation activity carried out by the enterprise's internal audit department. It is used to evaluate the effectiveness of the enterprise's internal control, the authenticity of financial information, and the rationality of operational activities, and put forward improvement suggestions. A is external audit, C and D are not internal audit in the sense of governance.

text.zh: What is the role of internal audit in corporate governance?
Helping the management cover up non-compliant behaviors
Evaluating and improving the effectiveness of internal control, and reducing operational and financial risks
Interfering with the daily operation and management of the enterprise
Reducing the transparency of the enterprise's operation

explanation.zh: *The core role of internal audit is to evaluate the effectiveness of the enterprise's internal control system, identify potential operational and financial risks, put forward improvement suggestions, help the enterprise optimize the governance structure, standardize business processes, and reduce risks. A, C, and D are opposite to the actual role of internal audit.

text.zh: Which of the following is a responsibility of the internal audit department?
Formulating the enterprise's development strategy
Auditing the enterprise's internal control system and putting forward improvement suggestions
Responsible for the enterprise's financial accounting work
Deciding the appointment and removal of the enterprise's employees

explanation.zh: *The responsibility of the internal audit department includes auditing the enterprise's internal control system, financial activities, operational activities, compliance with laws and regulations, etc., and putting forward targeted improvement suggestions to help the enterprise improve its governance level. A, C, and D are not the responsibilities of the internal audit department.

text.zh: What is the requirement for the independence of the internal audit department?
The internal audit department is directly managed by the management
The internal audit department is independent of the management and reports directly to the board of directors or the board of supervisors
The internal audit department must accept the leadership of the financial department
The internal audit department can only audit the departments below the management level

explanation.zh: *The independence of the internal audit department is the premise of ensuring the objectivity and fairness of the audit work. The internal audit department must be independent of the management (the object of supervision) and report directly to the board of directors or the board of supervisors, so as to avoid being interfered by the management in the audit work. A, C, and D damage the independence of the internal audit department.

text.zh: What does "corporate governance reform" refer to?
The enterprise adjusts its product structure and business scope
The enterprise optimizes its governance structure, improves internal control and information disclosure, and enhances the effectiveness of governance
The enterprise replaces its management team
The enterprise merges with other enterprises

explanation.zh: *Corporate governance reform refers to the enterprise aiming at improving the level of corporate governance, optimizing the governance structure (such as adjusting the board structure, improving the role of independent directors), improving the internal control system, enhancing the transparency of information disclosure, and solving existing governance problems, so as to enhance the effectiveness of corporate governance and promote the sustainable development of the enterprise. A, C, and D are not corporate governance reforms.

text.zh: Which of the following is a common content of corporate governance reform?
Increasing the enterprise's investment in R&D
Optimizing the board structure and increasing the proportion of independent directors
Expanding the enterprise's production scale
Improving the enterprise's marketing strategy

explanation.zh: *Optimizing the board structure (such as increasing the proportion of independent directors, improving the diversity of the board), improving the internal control system, strengthening information disclosure, and improving the incentive and restraint mechanism of the management are common contents of corporate governance reform. A, C, and D are operational reforms of the enterprise, not governance reforms.

text.zh: What is the purpose of corporate governance reform?
To reduce the enterprise's operating costs in the short term
To improve the enterprise's governance level, reduce risks, and enhance long-term competitiveness
To meet the requirements of regulators perfunctorily
To replace the existing management team

explanation.zh: *The purpose of corporate governance reform is to solve the existing problems in the enterprise's governance structure and mechanism, improve the effectiveness of governance, strengthen internal supervision, reduce operational and compliance risks, protect the interests of all stakeholders, and enhance the enterprise's long-term competitiveness and sustainable development ability. A, C, and D are not the purpose of corporate governance reform.

text.zh: Which of the following is a sign that corporate governance reform is effective?
The enterprise's short-term operating performance has improved significantly
The board of directors' decision-making is more scientific, and the internal control is more effective
The number of employees of the enterprise has increased
The enterprise's product sales volume has increased

explanation.zh: *The effectiveness of corporate governance reform is mainly reflected in the improvement of the governance level, such as more scientific and transparent decision-making of the board of directors, more effective internal control, better protection of shareholder rights and interests, and reduction of operational risks. A, C, and D are indicators of operational performance, which cannot directly reflect the effectiveness of governance reform.

text.zh: What is the meaning of "shareholder activism" in corporate governance?
Shareholders passively accept the decisions of the board of directors and management
Shareholders actively participate in the governance of the enterprise, put forward proposals, and supervise the behavior of the board of directors and management
Shareholders interfere in the daily operation of the enterprise
Shareholders demand that the enterprise pay high dividends regardless of the enterprise's development needs

explanation.zh: *Shareholder activism refers to shareholders (especially institutional shareholders) actively participating in the corporate governance process, such as putting forward proposals at shareholders' meetings, voting on important decisions, supervising the behavior of the board of directors and management, and promoting the enterprise to improve its governance level and protect shareholder interests. A, C, and D are not the correct understanding of shareholder activism.

text.zh: Which of the following is an example of shareholder activism?
Institutional shareholders put forward a proposal to optimize the executive compensation system at the shareholders' meeting
Shareholders ignore the decisions of the shareholders' meeting
Shareholders sell their shares because they are dissatisfied with the enterprise's performance
Shareholders demand that the enterprise change its business scope

explanation.zh: *Institutional shareholders putting forward proposals to optimize the executive compensation system, improve the board structure, or oppose improper decisions of the management at the shareholders' meeting is a typical example of shareholder activism. This behavior helps to promote the enterprise to improve its governance level. B, C, and D are not examples of shareholder activism.

text.zh: What is the impact of shareholder activism on corporate governance?
Interfering with the normal decision-making of the enterprise
Promoting the enterprise to improve its governance level and protect shareholder interests
Reducing the efficiency of the enterprise's decision-making
Causing conflicts between shareholders and management

explanation.zh: *Moderate shareholder activism can promote the enterprise to standardize its decision-making process, improve the transparency of information disclosure, strengthen the supervision of the management, and protect the legitimate rights and interests of shareholders, which is conducive to improving the level of corporate governance. A, C, and D are the negative impacts of excessive shareholder activism, not the general impact.

text.zh: What does "corporate governance principles" refer to?
A set of rules formulated by the enterprise to regulate employees' behavior
A set of guiding principles and norms for corporate governance formulated by international organizations or regulatory authorities
A set of standards for evaluating the enterprise's operating performance
A set of norms for the enterprise's environmental protection

explanation.zh: *Corporate governance principles are a set of guiding principles and norms for corporate governance formulated by international organizations (such as the OECD) or national regulatory authorities, which cover board governance, shareholder rights protection, information disclosure, internal control and other aspects, and guide enterprises to establish a sound corporate governance structure. A, C, and D are not corporate governance principles.

text.zh: Which of the following is a core content of the OECD Corporate Governance Principles?
Enterprise's environmental protection requirements
Enterprise's employee welfare standards
Protection of shareholder rights and interests, and the role of the board of directors
Enterprise's product quality standards

explanation.zh: *The core content of the OECD Corporate Governance Principles includes protecting shareholder rights and interests, ensuring the equitable treatment of all shareholders, strengthening the role of the board of directors, improving information disclosure and transparency, and respecting the rights of other stakeholders. A, B, and D are not core contents of the OECD Corporate Governance Principles.

text.zh: What is the role of corporate governance principles?
Forcing enterprises to adopt a unified governance model
Providing a reference framework for enterprises to establish and improve their corporate governance structure
Restricting the independent decision-making power of enterprises
Increasing the operating costs of enterprises

explanation.zh: *Corporate governance principles provide a scientific and reasonable reference framework for enterprises, guiding enterprises to establish and improve their corporate governance structure, standardize their governance behavior, and improve their governance level. They do not force enterprises to adopt a unified model, but allow enterprises to adjust according to their own actual situation. A, C, and D are opposite to the actual role.

text.zh: What is the meaning of "compliance committee" in corporate governance?
A committee responsible for the enterprise's production and operation
A special committee established by the enterprise to be responsible for compliance management, formulate compliance policies, and supervise compliance work
A committee responsible for the enterprise's financial management
A committee responsible for the enterprise's human resource management

explanation.zh: *The compliance committee is a special committee under the board of directors (or directly under the management) of the enterprise, which is responsible for formulating the enterprise's compliance policies and strategies, supervising the implementation of compliance management, investigating compliance risks, and ensuring that the enterprise's operation complies with laws, regulations and internal rules. A, C, and D are not the functions of the compliance committee.

text.zh: Which of the following is a responsibility of the compliance committee?
Formulating the enterprise's marketing strategy
Investigating and handling the enterprise's non-compliant behaviors
Deciding the enterprise's annual financial budget
Responsible for the enterprise's employee training

explanation.zh: *The responsibilities of the compliance committee include formulating compliance policies, conducting compliance training, supervising the implementation of compliance work, investigating non-compliant behaviors of the enterprise and its employees, and putting forward rectification suggestions. A, C, and D are not the responsibilities of the compliance committee.

text.zh: What is the requirement for the composition of the compliance committee?
The compliance committee must be composed of the enterprise's management
The compliance committee should include independent directors and professionals with legal, compliance and other backgrounds
The compliance committee must be composed of external experts
The compliance committee can be composed of any employees of the enterprise

explanation.zh: *To ensure the independence and professionalism of the compliance committee, its members should include independent directors (to ensure objectivity) and professionals with legal, compliance, financial and other backgrounds (to ensure professional judgment), so as to effectively perform the compliance supervision function. A, C, and D do not meet the composition requirements of the compliance committee.

text.zh: What is the meaning of "board remuneration committee" in corporate governance?
A committee responsible for the enterprise's employee salary management
A special committee of the board of directors responsible for formulating the executive compensation system and evaluating the performance of the management
A committee responsible for the enterprise's financial expenditure management
A committee responsible for the enterprise's bonus distribution

explanation.zh: *The board remuneration committee is a special committee of the board of directors, mainly responsible for formulating and reviewing the compensation system of the enterprise's senior management and directors, evaluating the performance of the management, linking the compensation with the performance, and ensuring that the compensation system is fair, reasonable and able to stimulate the management. A, C, and D are not the functions of the board remuneration committee.

text.zh: Which of the following is a responsibility of the board remuneration committee?
Deciding the salary of ordinary employees
Formulating the executive compensation plan and submitting it to the board of directors for approval
Responsible for the enterprise's financial accounting work
Supervising the daily operation of the management

explanation.zh: *The core responsibility of the board remuneration committee is to formulate the compensation plan for the enterprise's senior management and directors, evaluate the performance of the management, adjust the compensation according to the performance, and submit the plan to the board of directors for approval. A, C, and D are not the responsibilities of the board remuneration committee.

text.zh: What is the benefit of establishing a board remuneration committee?
Reducing the enterprise's labor costs
Ensuring the fairness and rationality of the executive compensation system, and reducing the agency problem
Increasing the salary of the management arbitrarily
Reducing the participation of the board of directors in executive compensation decisions

explanation.zh: *Establishing a board remuneration committee can make the formulation of the executive compensation system more professional, fair and transparent, link the executive compensation with the enterprise's performance and long-term development, reduce the agency conflict between the management and shareholders, and stimulate the management to work hard for the enterprise's development. A, C, and D are opposite to the actual benefit.

text.zh: What does "board nomination committee" in corporate governance refer to?
A committee responsible for the enterprise's employee recruitment
A special committee of the board of directors responsible for recommending candidates for directors and senior management
A committee responsible for the enterprise's talent training
A committee responsible for the enterprise's organizational structure adjustment

explanation.zh: *The board nomination committee is a special committee of the board of directors, mainly responsible for formulating the criteria for the selection of directors and senior management, recommending qualified candidates for directors and senior management, and ensuring that the board of directors and management have the necessary professional ability and integrity to perform their duties. A, C, and D are not the functions of the board nomination committee.

text.zh: Which of the following is a responsibility of the board nomination committee?
Deciding the appointment of ordinary employees
Evaluating the qualifications of candidates for directors and senior management
Responsible for the enterprise's talent training plan
Formulating the enterprise's development strategy

explanation.zh: *The responsibilities of the board nomination committee include formulating the selection criteria for directors and senior management, searching for and evaluating qualified candidates, recommending candidates to the board of directors, and evaluating the performance of existing directors and senior management. A, C, and D are not the responsibilities of the board nomination committee.

text.zh: What is the role of the board nomination committee in corporate governance?
Ensuring that the board of directors and management have the necessary professional ability and integrity
Reducing the number of directors and senior management
Increasing the salary of directors and senior management
Interfering with the decision-making of the board of directors

explanation.zh: *The core role of the board nomination committee is to select qualified directors and senior management for the enterprise, ensure that the board of directors and management have the professional ability, experience and integrity required to perform their duties, improve the overall quality of the board of directors and management, and promote the standardized operation of the enterprise. B, C, and D are opposite to the actual role.

text.zh: Which of the following is NOT a core purpose of investor Engagement?
Improving the ESG performance of invested enterprises
Reducing ESG-related risks of the investment portfolio
Obtaining excess returns through short-term speculation
Enhancing the long-term value creation capacity of the investment portfolio
What is the primary difference between active ownership and negative screening?
Active ownership focuses on short-term returns, while negative screening focuses on long-term returns
Active ownership proactively influences enterprises, while negative screening passively excludes assets
Active ownership ignores ESG factors, while negative screening prioritizes ESG factors
Active ownership involves selling assets, while negative screening involves buying assets
Which of the following best describes the concept of stewardship in the context of active ownership?
The obligation of investors to maximize short-term profits for shareholders
The responsibility of investors to monitor and influence invested companies to protect long-term value
The practice of selling underperforming assets to reduce portfolio risk
The process of selecting assets based on their past ESG performance
Which of the following is a common form of investor engagement with invested companies?
Ignoring communication with company management
Holding regular meetings with company executives to discuss ESG issues
Only relying on public reports to assess company performance
Refusing to vote on corporate governance proposals
What is the purpose of escalation techniques in active ownership?
To end engagement with a company immediately
To increase pressure on a company that fails to respond to initial engagement efforts
To reduce the level of investor involvement in company affairs
To focus solely on short-term financial gains
Which of the following is an example of a shareholder resolution in the context of active ownership?
A proposal submitted by shareholders requesting the company to disclose its carbon emissions targets
A decision by the company’s board to increase dividend payments
A request by management to shareholders to approve a new CEO
A plan by investors to sell all their shares in the company
Which of the following best describes the benefit of active ownership for investors?
Eliminating all investment risks
Improving the risk-adjusted returns of the investment portfolio
Guaranteeing short-term profits
Reducing the need for ESG analysis
What is a potential limitation of investor engagement?
It requires significant time and resources to implement effectively
It always leads to immediate improvements in company ESG performance
It eliminates the need for portfolio diversification
It guarantees higher returns than passive investing
Which of the following stakeholders is NOT typically involved in investor engagement processes?
Company management and board of directors
Other institutional investors
Individual retail investors
Competitors of the invested company
How does collaborative engagement differ from individual engagement?
Collaborative engagement involves only one investor, while individual engagement involves multiple investors
Collaborative engagement involves multiple investors working together to engage a company, while individual engagement is done by a single investor
Collaborative engagement focuses on short-term goals, while individual engagement focuses on long-term goals
Collaborative engagement is less effective than individual engagement
Which of the following is a key principle of effective stewardship according to CFA ESG v7?
Prioritizing short-term profits over long-term value
Regular monitoring of invested companies’ ESG and governance performance
Avoiding any communication with company management
Focusing solely on financial metrics
Which of the following is NOT a form of escalation in active ownership?
Filing a shareholder resolution
Publicly criticizing the company’s ESG practices
Increasing holdings in the company
Divesting from the company
What role does voting play in active ownership?
It is a passive strategy that has no impact on company decisions
It allows investors to express their views on corporate governance and ESG proposals
It is only used to approve dividend payments
It eliminates the need for direct engagement with management
Which of the following best describes the relationship between active ownership and ESG integration?
Active ownership and ESG integration are mutually exclusive strategies
ESG integration provides the analysis needed for effective active ownership
Active ownership focuses on financial metrics, while ESG integration focuses on non-financial metrics
ESG integration is a form of active ownership
What is a key challenge of engaging with private companies (compared to public companies) in active ownership?
Private companies have no ESG risks
Private companies are more transparent about their ESG practices
Private companies often have less public disclosure of ESG information
Private companies are required to hold annual general meetings with shareholders
Which of the following is an example of a governance issue addressed through active ownership?
A company’s carbon emissions
A company’s labor practices in its supply chain
A lack of independent directors on the company’s board
A company’s water usage
How do investors measure the effectiveness of their engagement efforts?
By focusing solely on short-term financial returns
By assessing changes in the company’s ESG practices and governance
By the number of meetings held with management
By the amount of money spent on engagement
Which of the following is a core responsibility of asset managers in terms of active ownership?
Ignoring the ESG performance of invested companies
Acting in the best interests of their clients when engaging with companies
Prioritizing their own profits over client interests
Avoiding any form of shareholder voting
Which of the following is NOT a benefit of collaborative engagement?
Increased influence on the target company
Shared resources and expertise among investors
Reduced costs of engagement for individual investors
Reduced accountability for individual investors
Which of the following best defines "divestment" in the context of active ownership?
Increasing holdings in a company to show support for its ESG practices
Selling all or part of a company’s shares due to unresolved ESG or governance concerns
Collaborating with other investors to engage a company
Filing a shareholder resolution to push for ESG changes
What is the role of proxy voting in active ownership?
It allows investors to elect company management directly
It is a way for investors to exercise their shareholder rights on key corporate proposals
It is only used for private companies
It eliminates the need for engagement with management
Which of the following ESG issues is most likely to be addressed through investor engagement?
A company’s historical stock price performance
A company’s failure to disclose its climate-related risks
A company’s quarterly earnings report
A company’s current market capitalization
Which of the following is a potential consequence of ineffective investor engagement?
Improved ESG performance of the company
Increased risk in the investor’s portfolio
Higher short-term profits for the investor
Reduced need for stewardship
Which of the following best describes the concept of "engagement escalation ladder"?
A sequence of increasingly aggressive engagement tactics used when initial efforts fail
A tool to measure the financial performance of engagement efforts
A list of companies that investors should avoid engaging with
A method to select companies for passive investment
Which of the following is an example of a social issue addressed through active ownership?
A company’s greenhouse gas emissions
A company’s board diversity
A company’s water pollution
A company’s deforestation practices
What is the difference between active ownership and shareholder activism?
Active ownership is a subset of shareholder activism
Shareholder activism is a more aggressive form of active ownership
Active ownership focuses on ESG issues, while shareholder activism focuses on financial issues
There is no difference between the two terms
Which of the following is a key factor to consider when deciding to engage with a company?
The company’s historical stock price
The materiality of the ESG or governance issue
The company’s market share
The company’s quarterly revenue
How do investors ensure that their engagement efforts are aligned with their fiduciary duties?
By focusing solely on short-term financial returns
By engaging with companies to promote long-term value creation
By avoiding any form of risk management
By prioritizing their own interests over client interests
Which of the following is NOT a common goal of investor engagement?
Improving the company’s ESG disclosure
Reducing the company’s long-term value
Enhancing the company’s corporate governance
Mitigating ESG-related risks
Which of the following is an example of environmental engagement?
Pushing a company to improve its employee diversity
Encouraging a company to adopt a net-zero carbon target
Advocating for better executive compensation practices
Requesting a company to improve its board independence
What is the benefit of transparency in investor engagement?
It reduces accountability for investors
It allows stakeholders to understand the investor’s engagement goals and actions
It increases the cost of engagement
It limits the investor’s ability to influence the company
Which of the following is a challenge of engaging with companies in emerging markets?
Stronger regulatory frameworks for ESG disclosure
Higher levels of ESG awareness among company management
Limited access to ESG information and weaker governance standards
Lower ESG-related risks
Which of the following best describes "engagement monitoring"?
Tracking the company’s financial performance after engagement
Following up with the company to ensure it implements agreed-upon changes
Selling shares in the company if engagement fails
Filing a shareholder resolution to push for change
Which of the following is a key principle of the UN PRI (Principles for Responsible Investment) related to active ownership?
Investors should avoid engaging with companies on ESG issues
Investors should incorporate ESG factors into their ownership policies and practices
Investors should prioritize short-term profits over long-term value
Investors should ignore the ESG performance of their portfolio companies
Which of the following is NOT an example of governance engagement?
Pushing for more independent directors on the board
Advocating for transparent executive compensation
Requesting a company to reduce its carbon footprint
Urging a company to improve its audit committee oversight
How does active ownership contribute to sustainable investing?
By excluding all companies with ESG risks
By driving positive ESG changes in companies and promoting long-term sustainability
By focusing solely on financial returns
By avoiding any form of engagement with companies
Which of the following is a potential benefit of engagement for the target company?
Increased regulatory risk
Improved ESG performance and reputation
Reduced access to capital
Higher operational costs
Which of the following is a key consideration when developing an engagement strategy?
The company’s short-term stock price movements
The investor’s short-term financial goals
The materiality of the ESG issue and the company’s willingness to engage
The number of shares the investor holds in the company
Which of the following best describes "proxy advice" in the context of active ownership?
Advice provided by the company’s management to investors on how to vote
Independent guidance for investors on how to vote on shareholder proposals
A strategy to divest from underperforming companies
A method to select companies for engagement
Which of the following is an example of a successful engagement outcome?
A company ignores investor requests to improve its ESG practices
A company implements a new diversity and inclusion policy after investor engagement
An investor divests from a company due to unresolved ESG concerns
A company’s stock price declines after engagement
What is the role of institutional investors in active ownership?
To avoid any form of engagement with companies
To use their large holdings to influence companies’ ESG and governance practices
To focus solely on short-term financial returns
To delegate all engagement responsibilities to retail investors
Which of the following is a limitation of using shareholder resolutions as an engagement tool?
They are too easy to pass
They require significant resources to prepare and promote
They always result in immediate changes to company practices
They are only available to retail investors
Which of the following best describes the relationship between active ownership and divestment?
Divestment is a form of active ownership, used as an escalation technique
Active ownership and divestment are mutually exclusive strategies
Divestment is a passive strategy that replaces active ownership
Active ownership always leads to divestment
Which of the following ESG issues is most likely to be material for a fossil fuel company?
Employee diversity in the tech department
Climate change risk and carbon emissions
Board diversity in the retail division
Water usage in the office building
Which of the following is a key component of an effective engagement plan?
No clear goals or objectives
A timeline for follow-up and monitoring
Avoiding communication with company management
Focusing on non-material ESG issues
What is the impact of active ownership on corporate behavior?
It has no impact on corporate behavior
It can drive companies to improve their ESG practices and governance
It always leads to a decrease in corporate profits
It forces companies to focus solely on short-term goals
Which of the following is an example of a collaborative engagement initiative?
A single investor meeting with a company’s management
A group of institutional investors jointly engaging a company on climate change
An investor filing a shareholder resolution alone
An investor divesting from a company due to ESG concerns
Which of the following is a key responsibility of investors in terms of stewardship?
To ignore the ESG performance of invested companies
To monitor and hold company management accountable for ESG and governance practices
To prioritize short-term profits over long-term value
To avoid voting on shareholder proposals
Which of the following best describes the future trend of active ownership?
It will become less important as passive investing grows
It will continue to grow as investors focus more on ESG and long-term value
It will be replaced by negative screening
It will focus solely on financial metrics
